newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies seesaw, close mixed after U.S. hike.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies seesaw, close mixed after U.S. hike.

text.p: IMM currency futures seesawed in erratic late pit trading to finish mixed after the Federal Reserve matched expectations and raised U.S. interest rates.

The Federal Open Market Committee meeting ended with an announcement that the central bank was tightening money market conditions slightly with the expectation that the Federal funds rate would rise 25 basis points to around 5.50 percent.
The discount rate remained unchanged at 5.00 percent.
The Fed said it acted in light ot persisting strength in demand that is increasing the risk of inflationary imbalances that eventually would undermine the economy's expansion.
It called the slight firming of monetary conditions, which analysts said was very well-telegraphed, a "prudent step."
"I think the news is fully discounted by the foreign exchange market," said Mike Malpede, forex analyst, Refco Inc.
He said he thought the dollar might have slight "downside vulnerability" very nearterm after the initial upside test faltered following news of the U.S. rate increase.
But he also looked for any currency rise to prove limited, with the dollar seen still bounded by familiar ranges and well-supported near 1.67 marks and 122.00 yen.
Those equal $0.6020 and $0.008294 in June marks and yen.
"This is the most widely anticipated rate hike in history," added Earl Johnson, foreign exchange economist, Bank of Montreal in Chicago. "It's totally discounted."

He said he looked for more dollar upside soon, given his expectations that the Fed will continue tightening into summer, when he expected the Fed funds rate to top out at 5.75 percent to 6.00 percent.
"This is the first of a series of tightenings," Johnson said, adding that he expected the dollar to garner support from the rate rises and head toward the 1.7210 mark level.
That would equate a fall in June marks to $0.5843.
Currencies might find some support, however, if U.S. Treasuries and equities pull back further, Malpede added.

On the trading floor, the initial kneejerk upside response gave way to a selloff to session lows as sellstops were triggered, brokers said. But then they said the banks entered buying and tugged futures back up again as trading turned erratic and spotty.
"There was not much paper business, and we hit sellstops but the banks put it back where it was," said a floor broker.
June yen pierced critical support at $0.008163, or about 123.97, before recovering and settling above there.
"It wasn't really all that bad, not too bad," agreed another floor broker of market conditions during the last 45 minutes of pit activity.

June yen ended down $0.000052 at $0.008184, marks eased $0.0009 to $0.5951, Swiss francs fell $0.0033 to $0.6884, sterling closed flat at $1.6178, Canadian dollar rose $0.0003 to $0.7295, Australian dollar slid $0.0073 to $0.7815, and Mexican peso rose $0.000400 to $0.122475.
